case.case_title: Dhammiaka Yapa v. Bandaranayake and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. 110/87, decided on 17 November 1987

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether Wijesekera was produced before a Magistrate as required by Article 13(2) and whether his detention was lawful.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed Wijesekera was detained for 109 days without being produced before a Magistrate, violating Article 13(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: Respondents denied mala fides and justified the detention orders under Emergency Regulations; they denied circumventing Magistrate's order.
key_facts: Wijesekera was detained under two successive Detention Orders under Emergency Regulations.
He was not produced before a Magistrate within 30 days as required by Article 13(2).
An application was made in Magistrate's Court to produce him, but he was transferred to Magazine Prison before the hearing.
Respondents denied that the transfer was to circumvent the Magistrate's order.
Statements supporting detention were recorded during the detention period.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) requires detainees to be produced before a judge within a reasonable time. The court noted the procedural irregularity but accepted the detention orders under Emergency Regulations as lawful preventive detention.
reasoning.application_to_facts: Although Wijesekera was not produced before a Magistrate within 30 days, the court found the detention orders issued under Regulations 17(1) and 19(2) justified by the circumstances and evidence.
principles_established: Detention under Emergency Regulations can be lawful even if procedural requirements under Article 13(2) are not strictly met.
Preventive detention orders under Emergency Regulations are not invalidated by non-production before Magistrate within 30 days.
precedents_cited: Nanayakkara v. Henry Perera and others

outcome.holding: The court held that despite non-production before a Magistrate, the detention was lawful under Emergency Regulations and did not violate Article 13(2).

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) protects detainees from unlawful detention without judicial oversight. The court's reasoning addresses this procedural safeguard and justifies the detention orders under the Constitution.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: Wijesekera was detained for 109 days without being produced before a Magistrate; an application was made in Magistrate's Court but he was transferred to Magazine Prison under a new detention order.
